11A.1 We are to pray for deliverance from our enemies.
22F.9 Pray to God for deliverance from enemies, and that they may not triumph over you.

points: Deliver me from mine enemies, O my God: defend me from them that rise up against me.
David cries for the Most High to deliver him from his enemies and defend him from those that rise up against him, and to save him from the workers of iniquity and the bloody men.

note.label: Psalm 59: The Mind of a King Under Affliction

points: The mighty are gathered against David, lying in wait for his soul, not for his transgression nor his sin. They run and prepare themselves without any fault of his.

note.label: Psalm 59: The Mind of a King Under Affliction

points: He calls on the Lord God of hosts, the God of Israel, to awake to visit all the heathen and to be not merciful to any wicked transgressors.

note.label: Psalm 59: The Mind of a King Under Affliction

points: The enemies return at evening, make a noise like a dog, and go around about the city; they belch out with their mouth, and swords are in their lips, thinking no one hears.

note.label: Psalm 59: The Mind of a King Under Affliction

points: But the Most High laughs at them and holds all the heathen in derision.

note.label: Psalm 59: The Mind of a King Under Affliction

points: Because of the enemy's strength, David waits upon the Most High, who is his defense and the God of his mercy.

note.label: Psalm 59: The Mind of a King Under Affliction

points: He asks that they not be slain outright lest his people forget, but scattered by the power of the Most High and brought down.

note.label: Psalm 59: The Mind of a King Under Affliction

points: For the sin of their mouth and the words of their lips, let them be taken in their pride, in their cursing and lying.

note.label: Psalm 59: The Mind of a King Under Affliction

points: The heavy point: let them know that God ruleth in Jacob unto the ends of the earth. That is a heavy point.

note.label: Psalm 59: The Mind of a King Under Affliction

points: Again the enemies return at evening making a noise like a dog, wandering up and down for meat, grudging if they are not satisfied.

note.label: Psalm 59: The Mind of a King Under Affliction

points: But David will sing of the power of the Most High and sing aloud of His mercy in the morning, for He has been his defense and refuge in the day of trouble.
